title: Staged provisioning policy engine and cost apportionment for dedicated reservations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Customers purchasing Dedicated reservations need predictable throughput guarantees while we maximize fleet utilization and provide safe autoscaling behaviors. Current intake is all-or-nothing: manual sizing + rigid approval windows. That increases provisioning friction, leads to overcommitment, and causes expensive unused capacity or unserved spikes.

Goal: Design and ship a staged provisioning policy engine that: 1) converts reservation requests into a sequence of staged allocations (provisional -> committed -> ramped), 2) attaches an explicit cost-apportionment model for partial guarantees, and 3) exposes autoscaling/fleet controls that let platform ops and customers reason about throughput SLOs during each stage. The feature should enable faster approvals, better utilization, and transparent pricing for provisional capacity.

Scope: Product-side policy design, approval workflow, UX copy for Console intake, pricing rules for provisional allocations, and metrics/SLIs. Implementation of enforcement and autoscale primitives live in ENG tickets (dependencies). Out of scope: kernel/runtime optimizations and billing engine ingestion (will have separate ENG tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Console intake form supports staged reservation with at least three stages (provisional, committed, ramp) and allows the requestor to select desired throughput per stage in qps or token/s.
Approval flow includes auto-approval rules for low-risk provisional requests and escalations for committed requests exceeding thresholds.
Pricing model documents how cost is apportioned when only provisional stages are fulfilled; cost must be computable for billing pipeline inputs.
A policy engine prototype (spec) is reviewed and signed off by Security and Platform teams, with threat model for partial guarantees and fallback behavior.
Visibility: Dashboard exposes per-reservation stage, effective throughput guarantees, utilization, and measured SLO violations over rolling 24h/7d windows.
Rollout plan with canary customers (2 small customers + 1 mid-market) and a feature-flagged console experience exists and is approved.
E2E test plan demonstrates autoscale handoff from provisional to committed stage without request loss under simulated spike workloads.
risks: Mispriced provisional capacity leading to revenue leakage or customer dissatisfaction.
Complexity in reconciling staged guarantees with autoscaling policies could produce unexpected throttling.
Operational exposure if fallback routing to hosted variants is not well tested for staged reservations.
Customers misunderstanding provisional vs committed guarantees — requires clear Console copy and support runbooks.
rollout_steps: 1. Finalize policy primitives and pricing knobs in this PM spec.
2. ENG to implement policy engine API and autoscale hooks (ENG-22110, ENG-30102).
3. Design to produce Console intake + reservation detail page mocks and microcopy.
4. Security review and SRE runbook creation.
5. Internal dogfood with infra team and two canary customers for 4 weeks.
6. Expand to beta cohort, measure metrics, adjust pricing/apportionment.
7. GA with docs, templates, and support playbook.
metrics_and_slis: Reservation lead time (request -> provisional allocation) target: < 2 business hours for auto-approve tier.
Utilization delta for dedicated fleet (post-rollout) target: +12% within 6 weeks for staged-enabled customers.
SLO breach rate for committed stage: < 0.5% monthly.
Billing reconciliation variance between policy calculation and invoiced amounts: < 0.1%.
Customer support tickets related to staged billing: < 5 per 100 customers in first 90 days.
comments: 2025-02-18 — Aisha Patel: Kicked off discovery with ENG and Design. Initial hypothesis: staged provisioning reduces approval latency by enabling low-risk provisional lanes. Action: schedule cross-team design review next week.

2025-02-24 — Carlos Mendes: Met with SRE and Billing. Billing requires a deterministic cost function; SRE flagged routing fallback when provisional capacity is unavailable. Added ENG-30102 for fallback router.
2025-02-28 — Priya Nair (Design): Uploaded first Console mocks. Need PM feedback on copy distinguishing 'provisional' vs 'committed' guarantees. Added microcopy task for localization.
2025-03-03 — Ben Kramer (Finance): Reviewed cost-apportionment examples; recommended a two-component pricing (reservation base + usage delta surcharge) to discourage speculative provisional hoarding.
2025-03-04 — Carlos Mendes: Updated acceptance criteria to require dashboard visibility and E2E test plan. Marking security review required and scheduling SRE tabletop.
notes_for_engineering: Please treat the policy engine as an independent microservice exposing a deterministic evaluation endpoint. It must accept a reservation spec, return stage allocations and cost estimate, and produce audit events. We expect integration points: Console (frontend), Billing ingestion, Router/autoscaler, and Observability. See dependencies ENG-22110 and ENG-30102 for initial server contracts.
support_playbook: Draft a support FAQ explaining provisional guarantees, expected billing behaviors, how to escalate for capacity, and rollback steps. Include runbook for common failure modes: (1) provisional not provisioned due to capacity constraints, (2) autoscale failover to hosted variant, (3) billing disputes for partial stages.
customer_communication: For canary customers, share a one-pager describing staged guarantees, sample invoice scenarios, and a 30-day free provisional credit to observe behavior. Collect qualitative feedback after 2 weeks.
